tagline: Global specialty chemicals and advanced materials leader serving batteries, adhesives, coatings and high-performance polymers
hero_kpi_rationale: The 14.5% EBITDA margin reflects Arkema's operational resilience amid demand pressures in Europe and the United States, supported by strong performance in High Performance Polymers and Adhesive Solutions despite a 190 basis point year-on-year contraction.

kpis.name: EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: EBITDA divided by sales, measures operating profitability before depreciation and financial expenses.
kpis.description: The EBITDA margin remains solid at 14.5% in the first half of 2025, reflecting the strong resilience of High Performance Polymers and Adhesive Solutions, partially offsetting the significant decline in Coating Solutions and Intermediates.
kpis.signal: EBITDA margin under pressure due to weak demand in Europe and the United States.

kpis.name: REBIT Margin
kpis.explanation: Recurring operating income (REBIT) divided by sales, excluding non-recurring items.
kpis.description: The REBIT margin declined by 280 basis points to 7.5%, reflecting the impact of higher recurring depreciation charges (335 M€ vs 297 M€) following the start-up of new production units in 2024, in addition to EBITDA compression.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in recurring operating income.

kpis.name: Sales
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from the sale of products and services before deductions.
kpis.description: Group sales amounted to €4.776 billion in the first half of 2025, down 2.1% on a reported basis, including a negative currency effect of 1.5%. At constant exchange rates, sales were nearly flat, down 0.6%, with volumes slightly declining by 0.7%, partially offset by a positive scope effect (+1.6%, primarily driven by the integration of Dow's laminated adhesives business).

kpis.name: EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, measuring operational cash generation.
kpis.description: Group EBITDA reached €693 million in the first half of 2025, down 13.5% compared to the same period in 2024 (€801 million). Results benefited from the resilience of High Performance Polymers and Adhesive Solutions, but were impacted by the significant decline in Coating Solutions and lower Intermediates performance compared to a high prior-year base. The EBITDA margin remains solid at 14.5% (16.4% in H1'24).
kpis.signal: EBITDA decline primarily driven by Intermediates segment performance.

kpis.name: Specialty Materials Sales Mix
kpis.explanation: Share of sales generated by the Specialty Materials segment (Adhesive Solutions, Advanced Materials and Coating Solutions).
kpis.description: The Specialty Materials segment represented 93% of group sales in H1 2025, a proportion comparable to 2024. Adhesive Solutions accounted for 30% (29% in H1'24), Advanced Materials for 38% (37% in H1'24), and Coating Solutions for 25% (26% in H1'24). Intermediates represented 7% (8% in H1'24).
kpis.signal: Specialty Materials sales mix stable around 93%.

kpis.name: Adhesive Solutions Sales
kpis.explanation: Sales of the Adhesive Solutions segment, specialized in adhesive solutions.
kpis.description: The Adhesive Solutions segment generated €1.431 billion in sales in the first half of 2025, up 3.2% compared to H1'24 (€1.386 billion), supported by the integration of Dow's flexible laminated adhesives business and resilience in construction and creative industries adhesives.
kpis.signal: Adhesive Solutions shows positive growth despite a challenging environment.

kpis.name: Net Income Group Share
kpis.explanation: Net profit after tax and interest, attributable to the group's shareholders.
kpis.description: Net income attributable to the group amounted to €96 million in the first half of 2025, down 57.1% compared to €224 million in H1'24. This decline reflects a 37.8% contraction in operating income (€219 million vs €352 million), including €69 million in exceptional charges mainly related to restructurings in Hydrogen Peroxide and the acquisition of Dow's laminated adhesives.
kpis.signal: Net income significantly lower due to exceptional charges and higher financial expenses.

kpis.name: Adjusted Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net income excluding the after-tax impact of non-recurring items for better comparability.
kpis.description: Adjusted net income (excluding the after-tax impact of non-recurring items) amounted to €217 million in the first half of 2025, down 38.4% compared to €352 million in H1'24, primarily reflecting EBITDA and REBIT margin compression in a context of weakening demand.
kpis.signal: Adjusted net income decline reflects operational margin pressure.

kpis.name: EPS Adjusted
kpis.explanation: Adjusted net income per ordinary share of the group.
kpis.description: Adjusted earnings per share stood at €2.87 in the first half of 2025, down 38.4% compared to €4.67 in H1'24, reflecting the decline in adjusted net income amid weak demand in Europe and the United States.
kpis.signal: Adjusted EPS decline in line with lower adjusted net income.

kpis.name: Currency Effect on Sales
kpis.explanation: Impact of exchange rate fluctuations on the group's reported sales.
kpis.description: The currency effect represented a negative 1.5% impact on sales in H1 2025, reflecting the weakening of the U.S. dollar and certain Asian currencies against the euro during the second quarter.
kpis.signal: Negative currency impact due to weakening U.S. dollar and Asian currencies.

kpis.name: Volume Effect on Sales
kpis.explanation: Impact of changes in sales volumes on group sales at constant prices.
kpis.description: The volume effect was -0.7% in H1 2025, reflecting a slight decline in delivered volumes compared to the prior year amid broadly disappointing demand in Europe and the United States, although partially supported by Arkema's growth in attractive sectors such as batteries, sports, electronics, efficient buildings and 3D printing.
kpis.signal: Volumes slightly down across most end markets.

kpis.name: Price Effect on Sales
kpis.explanation: Impact of changes in average selling prices on group sales at constant volumes.
kpis.description: The price effect stood at -1.5% in H1 2025, reflecting in the second quarter the impact of market conditions, geographic mix and the evolution of certain raw materials on the group's weighted average selling prices.
kpis.signal: Negative price effect due to unfavorable market conditions.

kpis.name: Scope Effect on Sales
kpis.explanation: Impact of acquisitions and disposals of entire businesses on group sales.
kpis.description: The scope effect was positive at 1.6% in H1 2025, primarily driven by the integration of Dow's flexible laminated adhesives for packaging, reflecting the group's strategic acquisitions in the Adhesive Solutions segment.
kpis.signal: Positive contribution from the acquisition of Dow's laminated adhesives.

risks.title: Increased competition in advanced materials
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the strategic context of strengthening the Advanced Materials segment through the acquisition of PIAM. The language is assertive and strategic, indicating strong competitive pressure in a high-value-added sector. The trend is upward due to intensified competitive investments in materials for electric vehicles and electronics.

risks.title: Dependence on specialized suppliers
risks.score_rationale: Although not explicitly detailed, the highly technical nature of advanced materials (e.g., polyimides, battery adhesives) implies a specialized supply chain. The risk is moderate but rising, linked to the product portfolio's premium shift and concentration of critical technologies.

risks.title: Increasing regulation on chemicals
risks.score_rationale: The chemical sector is subject to strict regulation (REACH, environmental standards, product safety). This risk is recurring, implicitly mentioned through compliance and sustainability issues. The regulatory language intensity in the sector justifies high severity, with an upward trend.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of industrial systems
risks.score_rationale: The risk is not explicitly mentioned, but factory automation and management of sensitive data (R&D, patents) make it an implicit issue. The chemical sector is a potential target. The trend is rising, in line with industrial digitalization.

risks.title: Intellectual property protection
risks.score_rationale: Recent acquisitions (PIAM, Polytec PT) are based on patented technologies. The mention of innovation as a strategic lever reinforces the importance of IP. The language is strategic and the risk is stable but critical, with high weight in high-value-added segments.

risks.title: Integration of strategic acquisitions
risks.score_rationale: The acquisition of PIAM (€728 million) and Polytec PT is recent and strategic. The integration risk is explicitly linked to future performance. The language is cautious but assertive, the trend is rising, and the weight is high for the specialization strategy.

risks.title: Exposure to climate regulations
risks.score_rationale: The group explicitly mentions climate issues in a dedicated note. Carbon regulation, decarbonization requirements for processes and the energy transition weigh on industrial costs. The risk is rising, with increasingly central language.
